name: Why does renovating an older home cost more than I expected?

mainEntity.name: Why does renovating an older home cost more than I expected?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost is determined by scope and existing conditions, not simply by the home’s age or square footage. Context: Elite Remodeling & Design may coordinate design, permitting, construction, and specialized work for kitchens, bathrooms, additions, ADUs, garage conversions, and whole-home renovations. Key factors: layout changes, structural reinforcement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, finish level, site access, and concealed damage. Practical guidance: compare proposals by included scope, allowances, exclusions, permit handling, and change-order procedures. Keep a contingency for conditions that cannot be confirmed before demolition. A phased approach may protect the budget while addressing the most important functional problems first.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older-home costs rise when demolition reveals outdated utilities, moisture, structural changes, poor prior work, or code-related upgrades. Compare complete scopes and exclusions, keep a contingency for concealed conditions, and consider phasing cosmetic work after essential repairs are defined.
